abstain: Abs + tenere: hold yourself away. Abstain from voting, from sugar, from the second slice.
Dry January: you abstain from wine. Keep your hands off it.
ameliorate: Melior = better (meilleur). Ameliorate: make it meilleur.
The “A-MELIOrate” team arrives to improve the slum conditions.
apathy: A + pathos: no feeling. Voter apathy: “Why bother?”
Apathy ≈ “a-path-y”: you don’t even walk down the path because you don’t care.
ascetic: Askesis = training. A monk who sleeps on a board and eats bread and water.
The ascetic’s room: a mat, a cup, nothing else. Self-denial for a higher goal.
avaricious: Harpagon hoarding gold: avarice = greed for money.
Avaricious sounds like “a very rich-ous” wish: always wanting even more.
belligerent: Bellum (war): the drunk who picks a fight in the bar.
A belligerent tone: shouting the first insult before the conversation begins.
circumvent: Circum + venire: go around the fence instead of through the gate.
The tax lawyer who circumvents the law finds the detour.
contrive: Con + trouver: you “find” (make up) a plan. A contrived plot feels forced, built to order.
Contrived = contrivance, a made-up gadget. An artificial happy ending.
delineate: De + linea: draw the lines. Delineate the border on the map.
A clear brief delineates who does what: every role outlined.
denote: De + nota: to mark. Red denotes danger; the dictionary meaning, not the feeling.
Denote = literal meaning (a rose denotes a flower); connote = associations (love).
derivative: Derive: flow from a river. A derivative film flows from other films with no fresh water.
In finance a derivative is derived from an underlying asset; in art a derivative work copies another.
derive: De + rivus (stream): to draw off from a stream. Derive meaning from the text.
Derive = tirer de: you draw a conclusion from the evidence.
disaffected: Dis + affection: love and loyalty gone. The voter who no longer feels part of any party.
Disaffected youth: bored, resentful, cut off from the system.
eclectic: Ek + legein: pick out. An eclectic playlist: jazz, techno and opera.
Eclectic = a buffet where you pick from many cuisines.
elucidate: E + lux (light): shed light on it. A good teacher elucidates the proof.
Lucid + ate: make lucid, make clear.
eminent: E + minere (to jut out): stands above the crowd. An eminent professor.
Eminent ≠ imminent. Eminent = distinguished; imminent = about to happen. Same “e” for “excellent”.
ephemeral: Epi + hemera (day): lasts one day. A mayfly, a soap bubble, a trend on TikTok.
The ephemeral beauty of cherry blossom: gone in a week.
fallacious: Fallere: to deceive. A fallacious argument looks sound but fools you.
A fallacy is a false step in logic. Fallacious = based on one.
forlorn: For + lorn (lost): completely lost, abandoned. A forlorn teddy bear on the road.
Forlorn hope: a mission with almost no chance. Sad, helpless.
frustrate: Frustra: in vain. To frustrate a plan: make it go for nothing.
Not just annoyed: bad weather frustrated our picnic = ruined it.
guileless: Guile = trickery (guile in French: guile ~ ruse). Guileless: no tricks. A toddler’s honesty.
“Guile-less” = “trick-less”: wears every thought on his face.
haughty: Haut = high: looks down his nose. The haughty maître d’.
Haughty ≈ « hautain »: chin up, nose in the air.
heretic: Hairesis = choice: you chose your own belief. Galileo, a heretic for the Church.
A heretic sits in the wrong pew: believes something against accepted doctrine.
immutable: In + mutare (change): can’t mutate. The laws of physics, immutable.
Immutable = set in stone: a statue never changes expression.
incongruous: In + congruere (agree): doesn’t match. A tuxedo at a barbecue.
Incongruous = a tuba in a string quartet: out of place.
insidious: Insidiae = ambush: creeps up on you. An insidious cough that slowly gets worse.
Insidious: a snake in the grass. Harmful, hidden, gradual.
itinerant: Iter = journey: an itinerary on legs. An itinerant preacher goes village to village.
Itinérant: a circus on the road. No fixed address.
jingoism: From a music-hall song “by Jingo!” in 1878: cheering for war. Flag-waving to excess.
Jingo is a harmless oath, but jingoism is militant nationalism.
jubilant: Jubilee: celebration. A jubilant crowd after the goal.
Jubilant ≈ « jubiler »: shouting for joy in the street.
juxtapose: Juxta = next to + pose: place side by side. Old and new buildings juxtaposed in Paris.
A comparison slide: two pictures juxtaposed so you see the difference.
languid: Languid ≈ langoureux: heat, a hammock, slow movement. A languid wave of the hand.
magnanimous: Magna + anima: great soul. The winner who shakes the loser’s hand.
A magnanimous boss forgives the mistake and moves on.
mollify: Mollis (soft) + facere: make soft. A free dessert mollifies the angry diner.
Think of a mollusc: soft. To mollify = soften anger.
negligible: Neglect-able: you can neglect it. A negligible difference of 0.01%.
Negligible = peanuts: so small it doesn’t matter.
panache: Panache = the plume on a helmet. Cyrano’s last word: « Mon panache ! ». Style with bravado.
Panache at the Oscars: the dress and the walk. Flair.
precocious: Pre + coquere (cook): cooked early. A child prodigy at the piano.
Precocious apricots: ripe in April. Skilled or mature before their time.
quotidian: Quotidian ≈ quotidien: your daily routine, nothing exciting.
The quotidian: the commute, the dishes, the emails.
refractory: Re + frangere (break): resists, like a wave breaking back. A refractory mule won’t move.
Refractory = « réfractaire »: the pupil who refuses all instruction.
rudimentary: Rudis = raw: a rudimentary shelter of branches, basic and unrefined.
Rudimentary skills: you know the ABC but not the sentences.
spurious: Spurius = illegitimate: a spurious claim has no right parent. Fake logic.
Spurious correlation: ice-cream sales and drownings both rise in summer, but one doesn’t cause the other.
staunch: Étanche: watertight. A staunch friend doesn’t leak your secrets.
Staunch supporter: stays loyal through every defeat.
subsume: Sub + sumere (take): take under a larger heading. Poodles are subsumed under dogs.
Subsume: absorb the small idea into the larger theory.
supplant: Sub + planta (sole of the foot): to trip up. Supplant the CEO by intrigue.
Supplanter: a young rival who takes the old star’s place.
tantamount: Tant + amount (monter): as much. A refusal tantamount to a no.
Tantamount = amounts to the same: silence is tantamount to a yes.
tenacious: Tenax: holding fast. A bulldog’s grip, a tenacious lawyer.
Tenir: you hold on. A tenacious stain won’t come out.
travesty: Travesti = dressed as something else. A travesty of justice dresses up unfairness as a trial.
A travesty: the cheap parody that mocks the original. A sham.
treacherous: Tricher: cheating friends, a treacherous betrayal; also an icy treacherous road.
Treacherous waters: calm on top, deadly below. Deceptive.
unequivocal: Un + equivocal: only one voice. An unequivocal yes.
« Sans équivoque »: no doubt at all, one meaning.
vehement: Vehere (carry): carried away by passion. A vehement protest.
Vehement ≈ véhément: a voice shaking with force.
vilify: Vile + ify: make out to be vile. The press vilified the minister.
Vilipender: you throw mud on someone’s name until it sticks.
